title.narrative: Restoring dignity and rebuilding lives for integrated protection in North East Syria

description.narrative: ltpgtIn response to the abrupt suspension of $118 million in US humanitarian aid, resulting in the collapse of nearly 90% of protection services in Northeast Syria (NES). Norwegian People’s Aid (NPA), in partnership with DAN for Relief and Development (DRD), proposes a six-month, lifesaving, integrated protection intervention. The project targets three of the most underserved and high-risk displacement camps: Al-Hol camp in Al-Hassakah, Twahina in Ar-Raqqa, and Abu Khashab in Deir-ez-Zor, collectively hosting over 65,000 vulnerable individuals, including women, girls, persons with disabilities (PwDs), and unaccompanied or separated children (UASC).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe intervention will directly reach 6,660 individuals and an additional 15,000 through strengthened community-based protection mechanisms. The response is tailored to local dynamics: Al-Hol camp presents high rates of UASC and early marriage Abu Khashab faces increased child labor and weak child protection systems Twahina suffers from acute documentation gaps and legal identity barriers. This context-driven design aligns with the 2024 Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) and the Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF) Reserve Allocation Strategy (RA3), ensuring responsiveness to critical and emerging protection risks in NES.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtCore Activities:lt/bgtltbrgtltbgt Case Management lt/bgtwill be provided by trained case workers for GBV survivors, PwDs, UASC, and high-risk individuals. Services include protection risk assessments, referral pathways, and structured case planning.ltbrgtltbgt Psychosocial Support (PSS)lt/bgt Individual PSS will be integrated within case management. Group PSS sessions are facilitated by trained PSS staff (with support from case workers as needed) and delivered using age-, gender-, and disability-adapted curricula focused on resilience and peer support.ltbrgtltbgt Legal Assistance lt/bgtwill focus on civil documentation (birth, marriage, death certificates) and family reunification to reduce statelessness and improve freedom of movement.lt/pgtltpgtltbgt Community-Based Protection (CBP):lt/bgt Community Protection Committees and the activation of PeaceAlert and Early Warning Early Response (EWER) systems will enable real-time protection threat identification and community-led responses.ltbrgtltbgt Explosive Ordnance Risk Education (EORE) lt/bgtwill be delivered by gender-balanced mobile teams targeting children, new arrivals, and high-risk populations in contaminated areas.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtStrategic Alignment:ltbrgtlt/bgtltbgt CO1_GP (General Protection):lt/bgt Enhances legal identity and documentation access.ltbrgtltbgt CO3_GBV:lt/bgt Strengthens survivor-centered GBV case management and psychosocial care.ltbrgtltbgt CO5_CP:lt/bgt Provides child protection case management, MHPSS, and family tracing.ltbrgtltbgt CO4_MA:lt/bgt Delivers lifesaving EORE to reduce injuries and deaths from explosive remnants.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtAAP is integrated across all phases of the project. During design, Community Protection Committees and focus group discussions ensured meaningful input from women, girls, PwDs, and other at-risk groups. Participation tools are adapted for illiterate individuals and persons with disabilities. A multi-channel Complaint and Response Mechanism (CRM) including help desks, hotlines, WhatsApp, and suggestion boxes is operational at all sites. Feedback is reviewed weekly by MEAL and protection teams, and emerging trends are analyzed monthly to guide adaptive programming. Staff receive ongoing training on ethical referrals, do-no-harm, confidentiality, and inclusive community engagement.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtNPA provides strategic oversight, compliance assurance, grant and financial management, and MEAL systems. DRD, with strong operational presence and community trust in NES, leads field implementation. NPA also coordinates safety and security. The project commits approximately 80.25% of the total budget to direct, life-saving protection services and community-based mechanisms. This includes case management, psychosocial support, legal assistance, EORE, staff salaries, essential supplies, and mobile deployments across three high-risk camps in Northeast Syria.ltbrgtlt/pgt
